title: Capacity Confidence Playbook — Predictive Dedicated Pools, Canary Surge Tests, and Graceful Fallbacks
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Purpose: Create an operational playbook and roadmap that makes dedicated pool autoscaling predictable and safe for customers. This ticket scopes the quarterly deliverable set: predictive health signals, a canary surge test suite, automated graceful-fallback policies, and an ops runbook for SRE/Customer Success. Goals: reduce customer-facing incidents caused by pool exhaustion by 60% quarter-over-quarter, establish a repeatable canary test cadence, and provide measurable SLOs for re-routing and fallback behaviors. Out of scope: billing model changes, long-term reservation pricing redesign.
milestones: M2: Instrumentation and dashboards deployed to staging (2026-03-05)
M3: Canary surge test harness + first run (2026-03-12)
M4: Runbook + playbook v1 on Confluence, ops rehearsal (2026-03-20)
M5: Beta customer rollout and telemetry validation (2026-03-31)
success_metrics: Customer-impact incidents due to pool saturation <= 3 per month after rollout
Median failover recovery time (route to fallback model) < 350ms
Cost variance from autoscale decisions < 8% vs baseline
Canary pass rate >= 95% for defined surge scenarios
Observability coverage: 100% of autoscale decision trees instrumented
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive prewarm reduces cold-start incidents but increases reserved cost; playbook will include signal thresholds to balance cost vs risk.
Decision: prefer model-variant fallback + regional failover over immediate horizontal scaling when burst duration < 120s.
Open question: should we expose an 'autoscale aggressiveness' knob to customers or keep defaults surfaced through tiers? — to decide by 2026-03-10.
Review feedback from SRE: add explicit throttling window to avoid oscillation during multi-region storms.
Action item: coordinate with Billing to ensure test traffic is not billed to customer trial credits (ENG-24011).
Risk: incomplete KV-cache warming may cause higher latency during canary runs; include KV warming checklist in runbook.
